findings.claim: The new CANCELLED -> RUNNING transition contradicts the function's own documented terminal-state invariant (INV-1) stated in the docstring just below it.
findings.failure_scenario: A caller cancels a task via transition(task, TaskState.CANCELLED), relying on the documented guarantee that 'A CANCELLED task has no outgoing transitions: cancellation is terminal (INV-1)' (lifecycle.py:26-27). With this diff, a later transition(task, TaskState.RUNNING) call now succeeds instead of raising ValueError, so a task believed permanently stopped can be re-activated and executed -- e.g. a worker that cancelled a task to free resources, then later re-dispatches it, unaware that cancellation is no longer terminal.
